title: Solving linear equations
subtitle: Undo one operation at a time to find the unknown.

explanation.title: Keep both sides equal
paragraphs: An equation is like a set of balanced scales. The left side has the same value as the right side.
The letter stands for a number we do not know yet. Solving the equation means finding that number.
To find the letter, undo the operations one at a time. Use the opposite operation each time.
Whatever you do to one side, do the same to the other side. This keeps the equation balanced.
Look at 3 + 2m = 17. The 3 is added on, so subtract 3 from both sides. This leaves 2m = 14. The m is multiplied by 2, so divide both sides by 2. This gives m = 7.
key_points: Undo each operation with its opposite.
Do the same thing to both sides.
Check your answer in the original equation.

interactive.title: Turn a story into an equation, then solve it
interactive.intro: Each example is a real-life problem with one unknown number. First we write the problem as an equation. Then we solve it one step at a time. Read the instruction on each card and click the highlighted part.

worked_examples.title: Solve b − 12 = −3
steps: The 12 is subtracted from b. Undo this by adding 12 to both sides.

worked_examples.title: Solve 3x + 1 = 7
steps: The 1 is added on. Subtract 1 from both sides: 3x = 6.
The x is multiplied by 3. Divide both sides by 3: x = 2.
